figures.alt: Interior load-bearing wall renovation with temporary shoring, exposed framing, prepared beam pocket, and protected work area
figures.caption: Structural renovation begins with a verified load path and a controlled temporary condition. Existing framing, loads, supports, beam design, connections, sequencing, and safety have to be resolved before a bearing element is altered.

figures.alt: Coastal home elevated foundation with reinforced concrete piers, structural beams, and open site access below the floor framing
figures.caption: Foundation decisions depend on the actual soil, water, existing structure, movement, loads, access, drainage, and repair approach rather than a generic symptom or a one-size-fits-all solution.

figures.alt: Second-story addition framing tied into an existing house with aligned wall framing, roof connection, temporary weather protection, and organized work area
figures.caption: The sequence matters: investigation, engineering, permits, protection, temporary support, selective removal, new structure, weatherproofing, inspections, services, and the restoration of finished spaces need a coordinated path.
